items.title: URL shortener
items.prompt: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly. Cover: requirements and scale estimates, API, how you generate short codes (collisions, length), storage, redirect latency, caching, analytics, and how you would handle 10x growth.
items.rubric: Functional and non-functional requirements, back-of-envelope numbers, key generation strategy (counter/base62 vs hash), read-heavy caching, DB choice justified, expiry and abuse handling.

items.title: Rate limiter
items.prompt: Design a distributed rate limiter for an API gateway: per-user and per-IP limits, algorithms (token bucket, sliding window), where the state lives, what happens when the store is down, and how to keep p99 latency low.
items.rubric: Compares algorithms with trade-offs, Redis or similar with atomic ops, fail-open vs fail-closed decision, headers and client feedback, hot-key concerns.

items.title: News feed
items.prompt: Design the home feed for a social app with 100M daily users. Cover fan-out on write vs read, ranking, storage of posts and timelines, celebrity accounts, pagination, and cache invalidation.
items.rubric: Hybrid fan-out, timeline cache, ranking service separation, handling hot users, cursor pagination, consistency trade-offs.

items.title: Chat system
items.prompt: Design a 1:1 and group messaging service (like WhatsApp). Cover connection handling (WebSockets), message ordering and delivery guarantees, offline users, read receipts, storage, and multi-device sync.
items.rubric: Persistent connections and presence, message IDs and ordering, at-least-once with idempotency, push for offline, storage partitioning by conversation, end-to-end encryption mention.

items.title: Load balancer internals
items.prompt: You work on a network load balancer. Explain L4 vs L7, how you would do health checks, connection draining, consistent hashing for sticky routing, and how the control plane pushes config to a dataplane running in 40+ regions without downtime.
items.rubric: Clear L4/L7 split, health check design (active/passive, hysteresis), graceful drain, consistent hashing, versioned config rollout with canaries.

items.title: Distributed cache
items.prompt: Design a distributed in-memory cache (like Memcached/Redis cluster). Cover partitioning, replication, eviction policies, consistency with the source of truth, thundering herd, and hot keys.
items.rubric: Consistent hashing, replication and failover, LRU/LFU trade-offs, cache-aside vs write-through, request coalescing, key splitting for hot keys.

items.title: Notification service
items.prompt: Design a notification system that sends push, SMS and email at 1M/minute with per-user preferences, deduplication, retries, and rate limits from third-party providers.
items.rubric: Queue-based pipeline, idempotency keys, provider abstraction with circuit breakers, preference store, DLQ and observability.

items.title: Metrics and alerting pipeline
items.prompt: Design a metrics system that ingests 10M data points per second from thousands of hosts, supports dashboards over the last 30 days, and fires alerts within 30 seconds. Cover ingestion, storage (time-series), downsampling, query, and alert evaluation.
items.rubric: Agents and batching, write-optimized TSDB, retention and rollups, query engine, alert evaluation loop, cardinality control.

items.title: Job scheduler
items.prompt: Design a distributed cron/job scheduler that runs 1M scheduled jobs a day exactly once, with retries, priorities, and visibility into failures.
items.rubric: Leader election or partitioned schedulers, durable job store, leases and heartbeats, idempotent execution, retry with backoff, admin UI/metrics.

items.title: File storage (Dropbox)
items.prompt: Design a file sync service like Dropbox. Cover chunking and deduplication, metadata vs blob storage, sync protocol and conflict resolution, sharing, and bandwidth optimization.
items.rubric: Block-level chunking with content hashes, metadata DB separate from object store, delta sync, conflict handling, notification of changes.

items.title: Search autocomplete
items.prompt: Design typeahead suggestions for a search box with 100M queries a day. Cover data structure, how top-k is computed and updated, personalization, latency budget, and sharding.
items.rubric: Trie or prefix index with precomputed top-k, offline aggregation plus near-real-time updates, caching, sharding by prefix, p99 target.

items.title: Payment processing
items.prompt: Design the core of a payment system that charges cards through a processor. Cover idempotency, double-charge prevention, ledger design, reconciliation with the processor, failure modes, and PCI boundaries.
items.rubric: Idempotency keys end to end, double-entry ledger, state machine for a payment, async webhooks and reconciliation jobs, tokenization to limit PCI scope.

items.title: Ride matching
items.prompt: Design the driver-rider matching service for a ride app. Cover location updates at scale, geospatial indexing, matching algorithm, ETA, and surge pricing data flow.
items.rubric: Geohash/quadtree or S2 cells, pub/sub for location, nearest-driver search with constraints, consistency during assignment, graceful degradation.

items.title: Key-value store
items.prompt: Design a distributed key-value store like DynamoDB. Cover partitioning, replication, consistency models, write path (WAL, memtable, SSTables), reads, compaction, and failure recovery.
items.rubric: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes, quorum reads/writes, LSM tree internals, anti-entropy or hinted handoff, tunable consistency.

items.title: Video streaming
items.prompt: Design video upload and playback for a YouTube-like service. Cover upload, transcoding pipeline, storage, CDN, adaptive bitrate, and how you would handle a viral video.
items.rubric: Async transcoding DAG, multiple renditions, object storage plus CDN, HLS/DASH, caching strategy for hot content.

items.title: API design review
items.prompt: You are reviewing a REST API for an orders service. Write the resource model and endpoints, explain versioning, pagination, idempotency for POST, error format, and when you would choose gRPC or GraphQL instead.
items.rubric: Clean nouns and verbs, cursor pagination, Idempotency-Key header, consistent error envelope, honest trade-offs between protocols.

items.title: Feature flags service
items.prompt: Design a feature flag system used by 200 services. Cover flag evaluation latency, targeting rules, staged rollouts, config propagation, audit, and what happens when the flag service is unreachable.
items.rubric: SDK with local cache and streaming updates, deterministic bucketing, kill switches, last-known-good fallback, audit log.

items.title: Log ingestion and search
items.prompt: Design centralized logging for 5,000 hosts producing 2 TB/day, searchable within seconds for the last 7 days and archived for a year.
items.rubric: Agents with batching and backpressure, Kafka-style buffer, indexing tier (inverted index), hot/warm/cold tiers, retention, cost controls.

items.title: Scale testing a dataplane
items.prompt: You need to prove a new release of a network dataplane handles 3x peak traffic before Black Friday. Design the load-testing setup: traffic generation, realistic mixes, environments, metrics to watch, pass/fail criteria, and how you make this repeatable for every engineer.
items.rubric: Production-like environment, traffic replay or synthetic generators, key SLIs (latency p99, drops, CPU), capacity model, automation and a go/no-go gate.

items.title: Webhook delivery
items.prompt: Design a reliable webhook delivery system for a SaaS product: ordering, retries with backoff, signatures, customer endpoint failures, replay, and visibility for customers.
items.rubric: Durable outbox, per-endpoint queues for ordering, exponential backoff with jitter and caps, HMAC signatures, dead-letter and replay UI.
